speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how old the patient is and describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions? When did you first notice them appearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped and pearly, and have you noticed any central dimpling or scaling on their surface? I would also like to know if the lesions are spreading in a linear pattern along the lines of scratching.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of pearly papules with central umbilication and the daycare exposure, this is highly suggestive of Molluscum contagiosum. I will confirm the diagnosis by requesting a visual assessment of the lesions. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The visual confirmation of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication, combined with the daycare exposure, is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
